jobs.description: Previous JobJob TitleAcademic Physiatrist (Asst, Assoc, or Full Professor - DOQ) Next JobApply for JobJob ID376515 LocationTwin Cities Job FamilyAcademic Full/Part TimePart-Time Regular/TemporaryRegular Job Code9403 Employee ClassInstr Fac/TC and Coord Cmp Add to My Favorite JobsEmail this Job About the Job Position Summary:The University of Minnesota’s Department of Rehabilitation Medicine is seeking a passionate, dynamic academic physiatrist to join our growing department, with a particular focus on expanding our neurotoxin services. This role offers a unique opportunity to shape the future of academic physiatry while delivering outstanding care within the M Health Fairview system.We are seeking a board-certified/board-eligible physiatrist who excels in patient-centered care, is committed to mentoring the next generation of providers, and brings a strong interest and experience in dystonia management and neurotoxin injections across a wide range of diagnoses.About the Role:As an academic physiatrist, you will play a vital role in the continued growth of our general Neuro-Rehabilitation program, which will serve as the primary focus of your clinical practice, with a significant neurotoxin and procedural practice embedded within your clinical portfolio. You’ll collaborate closely with the PM&R leadership to enhance interdisciplinary care and expand services across the system, and support strategic program development.You’ll also contribute to the education of medical students, residents, and fellows, and have the opportunity to engage in research and scholarly activities that align with your interests and the department’s strategic goals.Key Responsibilities:Expand neurotoxin procedural care for a wide range of rehabilitation needs, including spasticity, dystonia, migraine, and other neurological or musculoskeletal conditions.Deliver comprehensive general physiatry care for a wide range of rehabilitation needs, including stroke, spinal cord and brain injury, amputation care, spasticity management, intrathecal baclofen pump management, prehabilitation, dystonia, and other complex neurological or medical conditions.Participate in call coverage for the acute rehabilitation unit on a rotating basis and provide cross-coverage for inpatient services as needed, such as for vacations.Build and maintain strong, collaborative relationships with referring providers and clinical departments.Support the academic mission through teaching and mentoring trainees, including medical students, residents, fellows, and other allied health professionals.Contribute to scholarly activities, including research and academic initiatives, in alignment with departmental goals. Qualifications Required Qualifications:Completion of an ACGME-accredited PM&R residencyBoard-certified or board-eligible with the American Board of PM&R (ABPM&R)Minnesota medical license or eligibilityAbility to obtain DEA certification (Minnesota)Eligibility for credentialing and privilegingStrong interpersonal and teaching skills About the Department The Department of Rehabilitation Medicine is committed to innovation, education, and clinical excellence. Our faculty work in a collaborative, multidisciplinary setting that fosters growth, research, and meaningful clinical impact. Learn more about our department at rehabmedicine.umn.edu. Pay and Benefits Pay Range: This 0.8 FTE, with the potential to increase to 1.0 FTE, if desired, faculty provider position is dually employed by the University of Minnesota and University of Minnesota Physicians and includes two salary components. Total salary is market competitive and based on AAMC salary benchmarks. Clinical salary, aligned with clinical effort, is provided through M Physicians. The base salary range for this 0.8 FTE position is $218,000 - $240,000, commensurate with experience, qualifications, and effort. Information about benefits can be found here: M Physicians Benefits and University of Minnesota Benefits.Time Appointment: 80%

jobs.title: Assistant Professor - Biology
jobs.description: Founded in 1854, Hamline was the first university in Minnesota and among the first coeducational institutions in the nation. Hamline University provides a world-class education for undergraduate and graduate students. Our faculty, staff, and students cultivate an ethic of civic responsibility, social justice, and inclusive leadership and service. Hamline University is an Equal Opportunity employer. Hamline University does not discriminate on the basis of race; color; religion; creed; sex; national origin; marital status; familial status; status with regard to public assistance; membership or activity in a local human rights commission; disability; age; protected veteran status; or any other status protected by applicable law in its education or employment programs or activities. The University will provide reasonable accommodations to qualified individuals with disabilities. The Division of Natural Sciences at Hamline University invites applications for a tenure-track Assistant Professor of Biology, with a specialization in the Scholarship of Teaching and Learning in Biology , to begin fall 2027. Biology faculty are scholars who collaborate to provide high impact experiences for our students including team-based active learning courses, course-based undergraduate research experiences (CUREs), and faculty-mentored summer research. Our emphasis on student-centered, evidence-based teaching has earned the Hamline University Biology Program gold-level recognition by the Partnership for Undergraduate Life Sciences Education (PULSE) . We are dedicated to building a diverse and inclusive educational environment, in full accord with the value that Hamline University places on its commitments to diversity, equity and inclusion . The program fosters an environment in which all members are supported and feel empowered to obtain their teaching and scholarship goals. The Biology major curriculum provides students with a broad foundation in biology through a two-course core, a deeper understanding of various sub-disciplines of biology in elective courses, and a capstone experience in their senior year. In addition to teaching and providing research opportunities for Biology majors, Biology Program faculty also teach courses that are part of the general education curriculum (e.g., first-year seminars, natural science courses for non-science majors) and teach courses and provide leadership for several other academic programs that intersect with Biology. The candidate hired for this position will be welcome to collaborate with academic programs outside of Biology that are relevant to their expertise and interests (e.g., Environmental & Climate Studies, Computational Data Science). Teaching responsibilities for this position will include regular teaching of two introductory courses: BIOL 1510 and BIOL 1520: Integrated Concepts of Biology I and II . This position also offers the candidate the opportunity to teach other existing or newly-developed courses related to their expertise. We are especially interested in candidates who study the scholarship of teaching and learning in a biology context . Tenure-track faculty at Hamline typically teach six courses per academic year, with a one-course reduction during the first year and a three-course release after a successful 3rd year review. Laboratory sections count as fractional course load equivalents. jobs.description: The Carleton Psychology Department is seeking candidates for a tenure-track Assistant Professor position in Developmental Psychology ( preferably with a focus on social, personality, and/or identity development in children) to begin September 1, 2027. The person hired into this position will teach five courses per year in Carleton’s trimester system (Fall, Winter, Spring). Carleton is a highly-ranked liberal arts college in Minnesota that enrolls intellectually curious and engaged undergraduate students. The College prioritizes excellence in teaching and provides a wide variety of professional development resources to faculty. Carleton is committed to developing its faculty to better reflect the diversity of our student body and American society. Candidates from population groups that are under-represented at the College are strongly encouraged to apply. For further information regarding our faculty and useful resources for prospective faculty candidates at Carleton College, please visit the Office of the Provost’s website . Carleton College does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, creed, ethnicity, religion, sex, national origin, marital status, veteran status, actual or perceived sexual orientation, gender identity and expression, status with regard to public assistance, disability, or age in providing employment or access to its educational facilities and activities. We seek candidates who can teach introductory psychology, psychological data analysis (statistics), mid-level courses in developmental psychology and a related subfield (e.g., multicultural, personality, or social psychology), research laboratory classes that include methods instruction and hands-on demonstrations, and upper-level seminar(s) in their area of expertise. The ideal candidate will work with undergraduate students in their research program. A completed Ph.D. in psychology is preferred, but applicants who will complete their Ph.D. by September 2027 will be considered. We are particularly interested in candidates committed to teaching a student body with different backgrounds and perspectives. Carleton’s Department of Psychology includes nine tenure-track faculty, two part-time permanent lecturers, an administrative assistant, an educational associate, and an animal colony supervisor (shared with the Neuroscience Program). We have 35-45 majors per class year, many of whom work for the department as teaching assistants, lab assistants, research assistants, and graders. The Psychology department is housed in a newly renovated space within an integrated science center, including specially designed teaching labs and classrooms as well as dedicated space for student-faculty research collaboration. To apply, please complete the online application at go.carleton.edu/carletonjobs . Your application should include: 1) a cover letter that highlights key elements of your background relevant to teaching and conducting research at a liberal arts institution and suggests courses (including new courses) that you could envision contributing to the current curricular offerings in the department; 2) a curriculum vitae; 3) a statement about your teaching philosophy and practice (including examples of pedagogical reflection and growth and demonstrated commitment to teaching students from diverse backgrounds at a liberal arts institution) (2-4 pages); 4) a statement about your research (including specific contributions to multi-author publications) and plans for establishing a sustainable and productive research program at a small, undergraduate, liberal arts institution (2-4 pages). Shortly after your application is received, you may receive a request for the contact information for three references, at least one of which should address your teaching. We will contact your letter writers directly to request their letters of reference through electronic submission. Additional guidance in applying for this position can be found at our job website . jobs.title: Assistant Professor of Native American and Indigenous Studies
jobs.description: The American Studies program at Carleton College invites applications for a tenure-track Assistant Professor position in Native American and Indigenous Studies to begin September, 2027. A Ph.D. in American Studies, Ethnic Studies, or Native American and Indigenous Studies is strongly preferred, though candidates with a Ph.D. in another field will be considered if candidates demonstrate extensive interdisciplinary training in a field closely related to Native American and Indigenous Studies at the Ph.D. level. The candidate should have a Ph.D. in hand, or expect its imminent completion, by the time the appointment begins on Sept 1, 2027. The position involves offering courses with a focus on Native American and Indigenous Studies as well as core courses in the American Studies program. Within Native American and Indigenous Studies, we particularly welcome candidates with expertise in Indigenous governance, literatures, arts and cultural expressions, disability studies, geography, carceral studies, or Dakota Studies. Service responsibilities will be primarily in American Studies, including contributing to a developing Native American and Indigenous Studies minor. Successful candidates will be invested in building reciprocal relationships with local Native nations and Native community organizations. Ideal candidates will have a demonstrated track record of socially-engaged research, likely in collaboration with Indigenous Peoples, and a commitment to the integration of Indigenous Peoples’ priorities and ways of knowing into their teaching and scholarship. To apply, please visit the Carleton College jobs website and complete the online application by submitting a cover letter, CV, a Teaching Statement that speaks to working with students from a broad range of backgrounds in a liberal arts environment, and the names of 3-4 references by October 19, 2026. Full letters of reference, sample syllabi, and writing samples will be requested later. One letter may be provided from an Indigenous community partner with whom the applicant has previously or is currently collaborating. Ph.D. must be in hand by the start of appointment. Carleton is a highly selective undergraduate liberal arts college with a student body of approximately 2,000. Located in the thriving two-college town of Northfield, Minnesota, it is forty-five miles from the Twin Cities of Minneapolis and St. Paul, a metropolitan area with a vibrant Native community. This position is part of a broader institutional commitment to expand capacity in Native American and Indigenous studies in recognition of Carleton’s location on Dakota homelands. The new hire will complement other faculty engaged in NAIS-related scholarship in American Studies, History, Religion, Sociology/Anthropology, and Environmental Studies . Indigenous engagement at Carleton is supported by a full time Indigenous Communities Liaison, a broad circle of interested faculty and staff, the resources of a multi-year Indigenous engagement grant to transform institutional practices, relationships with supportive Indigenous community partners, and an active student organization, the Indigenous Peoples Alliance. The expected starting salary range for this position is between $87,480 - $93,290 . jobs.title: Assistant Professor of Neuroscience
jobs.description: The Neuroscience Program at Carleton College invites applications for a tenure-track position, to begin September 1, 2027, at the rank of assistant professor. We welcome applications from candidates with a PhD in neuroscience or a related field, particularly those with expertise in electrophysiology. Responsibilities include shared teaching of Foundations in Neuroscience with accompanying laboratory, an upper-level Neurobiology course with accompanying laboratory and a seminar in the candidate’s area of expertise. The typical teaching load is five courses spread over our three 10-week terms per year. We seek applicants who are committed to furthering the College’s goals of providing an effective learning environment for all students. A completed Ph.D. in Neuroscience or a related field with postdoctoral experience is preferred, but applications who will complete their Ph.D. by September 2027 will be considered. The successful candidate will demonstrate a strong commitment to teaching and research with undergraduate students in a liberal arts environment. Neuroscience faculty are expected to develop an active research program that engages Carleton undergraduates in scholarly contributions to their subfield. The College offers support for faculty research programs, including research facilities, student stipends and support for grant writing. In addition, support for all aspects of faculty work is provided by a college mentoring program, cohort activities for new faculty, Provost Office support, and extensive optional programming by our Perlman Center for Learning and Teaching . Carleton is committed to developing its faculty to better reflect the breadth of our student body and American society. Groups historically under-represented at Carleton are strongly encouraged to apply. Carleton is a highly selective liberal arts college with a curious and enthusiastic student body of approximately 2,000 undergraduates. We are committed to cultivating a welcoming, supportive, and diverse community, including meeting 100% of demonstrated financial need for all students, with 58% of students receiving need-based grants and scholarships. Of our domestic students, 32% identify as people of color; an additional 11% of students come from outside the United States. Located in the thriving two-college town of Northfield, Minnesota, Carleton College is forty-five miles from the Twin Cities of Minneapolis and St. Paul, within easy reach of a vibrant metropolitan area that is home to three million people and rich cultural resources. The Neuroscience Program at Carleton is jointly administered by faculty in Neuroscience, Biology and Psychology. We are housed in Carleton’s Integrated Science center with state-of-the-art research and teaching laboratories and equipment. For further information please consult the program website at https://apps.carleton.edu/curricular/neuroscience/ or email the director, Sarah Meerts (smeerts@carleton.edu). To apply, please complete the online application at go.carleton.edu/carletonjobs . Your application should include: 1) a cover letter that also speaks to courses (including new courses) that you could envision contributing to the current curricular offerings in the program; 2) a curriculum vitae; 3) a statement about teaching in an undergraduate liberal arts environment and how you would contribute to a college community that embraces a broad range of people and perspectives as one of its core values; 4) a detailed description of your plans for research with undergraduate students; and 5) After passing through an initial selection process, applicants may receive a request for the contact information for three references. We will contact your letter-writers directly to request their electronic submissions. Additional guidance in applying for this position can be found at https://www.carleton.edu/neuroscience/faculty-hiring/ . jobs.description: The Department of Theater and Dance at Carleton College invites applicants for a tenure track position in theatrical design to begin in the fall of 2027. An MFA or commensurate professional experience is required. The search committee seeks a dynamic professional artist who is committed to developing an inclusive pedagogy, rooted in a commitment to diversity and student transformation within a liberal arts context. This faculty member will develop and lead the theatrical design focus of the major and teach courses in multiple design/production areas with a primary focus in either scenic or costume design. Ideal candidates will have experience designing productions for both theater and dance. Carleton operates on a 10-week trimester calendar, with tenure track positions teaching the equivalent of five courses during the year. As part of the 5-course teaching load, the candidate will also design on the production season and provide mentorship for student designers. The appointment will begin on September 1, 2027. We are particularly interested in candidates committed to teaching a diverse student body. Carleton is committed to developing its faculty to better reflect the diversity of our student body and American society. Women and members of underrepresented population groups at Carleton are strongly encouraged to apply. The following materials are required: letter of application; curriculum vitae; creative portfolio (link to online portfolio is sufficient); a statement about teaching students from diverse backgrounds in an undergraduate, residential liberal arts environment. After passing through an initial screening process, applicants may receive a request for the contact information for three references, including at least one who is able to specifically address teaching experience. Review of applications will begin on September 1st, 2026 and will continue until the position is filled . All application materials can be submitted here . Carleton College does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, creed, ethnicity, religion, sex, national origin, marital status, veteran status, actual or perceived sexual orientation, gender identity and expression, status with regard to public assistance, disability, or age in providing employment or access to its educational facilities and activities. The expected starting salary range is $87,480 - $91,460. Actual pay will be adjusted based on job-related factors permitted by law, such as experience and training; licensure and certifications; market factors; departmental budgets; and responsibility. jobs.title: Assistant Professor/Professor of Practice/Instructor - Marketing & Management
jobs.description: Founded in 1854, Hamline was the first university in Minnesota and among the first coeducational institutions in the nation. Hamline University provides a world-class education for undergraduate and graduate students. Our faculty, staff, and students cultivate an ethic of civic responsibility, social justice, and inclusive leadership and service. Hamline University is an Equal Opportunity employer. Hamline University does not discriminate on the basis of race; color; religion; creed; sex; national origin; marital status; familial status; status with regard to public assistance; membership or activity in a local human rights commission; disability; age; protected veteran status; or any other status protected by applicable law in its education or employment programs or activities. The University will provide reasonable accommodations to qualified individuals with disabilities. The Hamline School of Business in Saint Paul, Minnesota, seeks applicants for an Assistant Professor or teaching track Professor of Practice or Instructor position in marketing and management. Our vision is to be the place “Where the business, government, and non-profit sectors intersect to educate and collaborate for the common good.” Our faculty, staff, and students cultivate an ethic of civic responsibility, social justice, and inclusive leadership and service. At the undergraduate level, the school offers a Bachelor in Business Administration with concentrations in accounting, business analytics, finance, management, and marketing and a Bachelor of Arts in Economics. At the graduate level, the school offers the following graduate degrees: Master of Business Administration, Master of Management and Leadership, Master of Science in Business Analytics, Master of Management and Leadership, Master of Public Administration, and Ph.D. in Management and Public Service as well as sequential degrees, dual degrees, and a joint MBA/JD degree with the Mitchell Hamline Law School. The School of Business designs its undergraduate and graduate program offerings to meet the needs of students who require the skills and knowledge to succeed in the rapidly changing realities of our local and global communities. The school is dedicated to preparing students to work across sectors to solve the complex issues facing today’s society. Faculty members play a pivotal role in developing new courses and management education certificates as well as ensuring a high level of learning through assessment activities. ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES Teaching and curriculum development responsibilities for the tenure-track position includes six courses per year (24 credits across the graduate and undergraduate levels), and the teaching faculty position includes seven courses per year (28 credits across the graduate and undergraduate levels). Potential course content areas include: Marketing Research Digital Marketing intelligence Marketing Automation and AI Foundations of Marketing Foundations of Management Operations Management Project Management Entrepreneurship Strategic Management First-year Seminar Course content matching the expertise of the applicant. - We are seeking candidates who have prior teaching experience (at least one semester) in some of these course content areas. - Preference will be given to candidates with familiarity and interest in AI technologies REQUIRED KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, ABILITIES AND KEY COMPETENCES Candidates must have demonstrable competencies in teaching. Candidates must be committed to the development of skills necessary for advising and mentoring students from culturally diverse backgrounds, and to the promotion and enhancement of diversity, equity, and inclusion in support of academic excellence. These practices include, but are not limited to instructional activities, curriculum content, and contextual framework. Experience teaching online is preferred Preference will be given to candidates with experience working with diverse student population

jobs.title: Assistant, Associate, or Full Professor in Large Animal Surgery
jobs.description: Previous JobJob TitleAssistant, Associate, or Full Professor in Large Animal Surgery Next JobApply for JobJob ID376702 LocationTwin Cities Job FamilyAcademic Full/Part TimeFull-Time Regular/TemporaryRegular Job Code9401 Employee ClassInstr Fac/TC and Coord Cmp Add to My Favorite JobsEmail this Job About the Job The Department of Veterinary Population Medicine (VPM) at the University of Minnesota College of Veterinary Medicine in St. Paul invites applications for a contract (non-tenure) full-time (100% appointment) faculty position in Large Animal Surgery. The appointment will be at the rank of Assistant Professor, Associate Professor or Professor at the University of Minnesota. The final rank and terms of appointment will depend on the qualifications and experience of the selected candidate consistent with Collegiate and University policies. Key responsibilities:Provide exceptional clinical service in Large Animal Surgery (LAS) at the Veterinary Medical Center, which includes the Piper Equine Hospital and Large Animal Hospital. Provide elective daytime services for large animal surgical and equine sports medicine/lameness cases, as well as emergent services and consultations to local veterinarians.Participate in evening/weekend/holiday on call coverage which is shared among 4 faculty. Provide clinical teaching and mentoring of veterinary students, interns and residents, and participate in resident training activities such as seminars, board exam preparation, and journal club.Provide didactic instruction of professional students to support the DVM curriculumDevelop close relationships with clients and referring veterinarians to provide comprehensive care and oversight for equine and food and fiber patients.Participate in scholarly activities and demonstrate a collegial, collaborative approach and willingness to participate in departmental initiatives, programs and committees. The clinical service is shared among 4 faculty. The caseload is approximately 90% equine with the remainder comprising llamas/alpacas, pet goats and pigs, with occasional sheep and cattle. The anticipated workload distribution is expected to be predominantly clinical service (includes daytime and after hours on call), teaching veterinary students in years 1-4 and training LAS interns and residents. Experienced surgeons are encouraged to apply. While scholarly activities are encouraged and expected, development of an independent research program is not an expectation of this position, nor is it required for academic advancement.The University of Minnesota seeks candidates who are interested in programs that support community and belonging and excellence of the academic community through their service, teaching, research, and outreach. The candidate will demonstrate commitment to delivering exceptional clinical service, teaching, student mentorship, and contribute to the national prominence of the Veterinary Medical Center, the VPM Department, and the University of Minnesota. About the Large Animal Surgery ServiceThe LAS service includes an enthusiastic, cohesive, patient-care oriented LAS team composed of four ACVS board-certified surgeons (one tenured, and three clinical), 3 house officers (2 surgery residents and 1 surgery intern), and 3 dedicated surgery technicians (along with additional 24/7 technical support). The clinical activities take place in the 50,000 square foot Leatherdale Equine Center (opened in 2007) which includes the Piper Equine Hospital, the Barenscheer Arena and the Nutrena Conference Center, and also at the Large Animal Hospital. The Piper Equine Hospital contains state-of-the-art surgical, and advanced imaging equipment, experienced support staff, and collegial colleagues. The hospital is well-equipped with a spacious OR that includes advanced surgical equipment (arthroscopic and laparoscopic towers, staplers and electrocautery devices for GI surgery, and AO compatible orthopedic equipment including locking plates) and a C-arm unit.

This full-time, annually renewable, contract (non-tenure track) faculty appointment is available immediately and represents an exciting opportunity to join a growing and collaborative specialty service within one of the nation's leading academic veterinary medical centers.We are seeking a colleague who is passionate about clinical excellence, teaching, collaboration, and advancing the field of nutrition. This position is anticipated to be associated with the Purina Veterinary Professorship in Nutrition, an endowed faculty appointment established to support excellence in veterinary nutrition education, clinical service, scholarship, and professional leadership. The professorship reflects the College's commitment to preparing future veterinarians to address the essential role of nutrition in animal health and welfare, strengthening the profession's ability to meet evolving societal needs, and advancing evidence-based nutritional care that promotes health, longevity, and quality of life for animals. The holder of the professorship will be expected to contribute to these goals through leadership in teaching, clinical service, research, mentorship, and outreach. What We OfferA collaborative and supportive academic environment.Opportunities to help shape the future of the Veterinary Nutrition Service.Exceptional specialty support and referral network.Access to advanced clinical technology and facilities.Opportunities for clinical, teaching, and scholarly career development.Competitive salary and comprehensive benefits package. Why Minnesota?The University of Minnesota Veterinary Medical Center is one of the largest veterinary teaching hospitals in North America, serving more than 40,000 small animal patients annually and supporting a vibrant community of specialists, trainees, researchers, and referring veterinarians. The Nutrition team works alongside specialists across 17 clinical disciplines and have access to advanced diagnostic and treatment technologies, including cone beam CT, advanced imaging, radiation therapy, MRI, CT, and other state-of-the-art clinical resources. The College of Veterinary Medicine is uniquely positioned within a major research university and offers extensive opportunities for interdisciplinary collaboration across the Academic Health Center, including partnerships with the Schools of Medicine, Dentistry, Public Health, Pharmacy, and Nursing. The Twin Cities provide an exceptional quality of life, combining nationally recognized healthcare systems, a thriving cultural and food scene, abundant outdoor recreation, and a strong biomedical and technology workforce. Location and Work Environment Work will be completed on the St. Paul Campus at the University of Minnesota – Twin Cities. In-person work is required for the clinical component of the position at the Veterinary Medical Center, largely during traditional Monday – Friday daytime hours. Didactic teaching is also done in person, though other aspects of the role may warrant flexibility for hybrid work. Work Schedule This position is full-time, typically Monday – Friday daytime hours. jobs.title: Assistant/Associate Professor of Counselor Education -State University Faculty
jobs.description: All Job Postings will close at 12:01 a.m. CT on the specified Closing Date (if designated). Working Title: Assistant/Associate Professor of Counselor Education -State University Faculty Institution: St. Cloud State University Classification Title: State University Faculty Bargaining Unit / Union: 209: Inter Faculty Organization City: St. Cloud FLSA: Job Exempt Full Time / Part Time: Full time Employment Condition: Unclassified - Unlimited Academic Salary Range: $64,963.00 - $193,146.00 Job Description Minnesota needs clinical mental health counselors and school counselors, and this program prepares them. We are looking for a counselor educator who wants real influence over how that happens. The Clinical Mental Health Counseling and School Counseling programs at St. Cloud State University invite applications for a tenure-track Assistant or Associate Professor of Counselor Education, beginning August 16th, 2027. We are a small faculty running daytime cohort programs with our own on-campus training clinic, live supervision, and a set of community partnerships that are already operating and open to a new colleague’s ideas. Because the faculty is small, your voice on curriculum, clinical training, and program direction will matter from your first semester – not your seventh year. We are open on specialty. We are seeking an excellent counselor who can contribute broadly across the CACREP core curriculum, not a candidate in any single subfield. Your particular clinical and scholarly expertise – whatever it is – will help determine what we build next. How teaching works here. A 3/3 graduate load . Graduate courses are weighted at 4 credits in the 24-credit IFO academic year-some clinical courses at five -, so a full graduate load is 6 courses per year rather than 8. Daytime only. Our programs run on a cohort model with daytime classes. Students know their full schedule from admission to graduation, and so do you. In counselor education, where evening teaching is the norm, this is unusual. No faculty member owns a course. Faculty submit teaching preferences annually. If you want to teach a course several years running to develop it, you can. If you want to move into something new, you can. We deliberately distribute the first-year content sequence – the heaviest teaching in the program, with intensive skills feedback and the beginning of gatekeeping – across the whole faculty rather than concentrating it on newer colleagues. You follow a cohort through its full three-year life cycle. You teach students in their first year, again in practicum, and through internship to graduation. Most programs don’t work this way, and it takes some getting used to. We do it because when you make a gatekeeping decision or write a recommendation, you’re drawing on three years of watching someone develop rather than one semester’s impression. A cohort’s first year typically includes Introduction to the profession, Ethics, Assessment in Counseling, Multicultural Counseling, and Counseling Procedures/Skills and either diagnosis and treatment planning or child/adolescent counseling. Summer is optional, and it’s yours. We poll students at orientation about which electives they want, and together with our advisory board build a 3-year summer rotation from that data. Faculty teach in their own areas of interest, so this is where specialization lives – the core curriculum is taught by everyone, and the summer sequence is where your expertise becomes curriculum. Because the rotation is built from student demand and planned three years out, you’ll know your summer teaching well in advance. Additional summer sections are also regularly available in our undergraduate program. Summer teaching is compensated separately from the academic year contract under Article 13 of the IFO agreement. Working Title: College Laboratory Assistant 2- Certified Flight Instructor- Fixed Wing Institution: Lake Superior College Classification Title: College Laboratory Asst 2 Bargaining Unit / Union: 218: Non-Unit City: Duluth FLSA: Non Job Exempt Full Time / Part Time: Part time Employment Condition: Classified - Unlimited Salary Range: $22.27 - $31.99 Job Description: This position provides the Center for Advanced Aviation (CAA), Professional Pilot Airplane and Helicopter programs, with tutoring, classroom assistance, student training, testing, record keeping, safety, security and technical support for the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) certified programs. The incumbent will serve as a Certified Flight Instructor, Chief and / or Assistant Chief Pilot (as required by FAA 141 Certification), and is responsible for direct, one to one flight instruction and leading students through: FAA required stage checks, preparation for end of course tests and proficiency checks. The CLA will be present and provide guidance to students during all pre-flight, in-flight and post-flight inspections and during all student flights. As required by the FAA, the CLA will be available by phone, radio, or other electronic means, when student flight training occurs. Salary Range: $22.27-$31.12 hourly. $46,500-$64,979 annually * Salary placement is dependent on education and experience. Annual rate will be prorated to actual hours worked Minimum Qualifications: Post-Secondary or industry certificate/diploma/degree or relevant licensure as a FAA 141 Certified Flight Instructor, Assistant Chief Instructor or a Multi Engine Instructor. One year of teaching and/or tutoring as a Certified Flight Instructor of initial Certified Flight Instructor Candidates or 4 years of work experience as a FAA 141 Certified Flight Instructor, Assist Chief Instructor, or a Multi Engine Instructor where no industry standard or an equivalent combination of education and work experience. Preferred Qualification: Demonstrated ability to work successfully with persons from diverse backgrounds, and commitment to diversity and inclusion initiatives. Hold a commercial pilot or airline transport pilot certificate and a current flight instructor certificate. The certificates must contain the appropriate aircraft category, class, and instrument ratings if required for the category and class of aircraft used; Flight training experience as a certified flight instructor, as a commercial or military pilot training program, or a combination thereof that must include: 1 year and a total of 250 flight hours; or 500 flight hours. The flight instructor instrument rating or rating with instrument privileges must include: At least 50 hours of flight time under actual or simulated instrument conditions; At least 500 hours as pilot in command; Instrument flight instructor experience, acquired as either a certificated flight instructor-instrument or an instructor in a military pilot flight training program, 1 year and a total of 125 flight hours; or 200 flight hours; For a course of training other than one leading to the issuance of a recreational or private pilot certificate or rating, or an instrument rating or a rating with instrument privileges, an assistant chief instructor must have: (1) At least 1,000 hours as pilot in command; and (2) Flight training experience, acquired as either a certificated flight instructor or an instructor in a military pilot flight training program, or a combination thereof, consisting of at least 11⁄2 years and a total of 500 flight hours; or 750 flight hours or an equivalent combination of education and work experience. Working Title: Computer Science Faculty Institution: Rochester Community and Technical College Classification Title: Community College Faculty Bargaining Unit / Union: 210: Minnesota State College Faculty City: Rochester FLSA: Job Exempt Full Time / Part Time: Part time Employment Condition: Unclassified - Limited Academic (Fixed Term) Salary Range: Job Description Rochester Community and Technical College is seeking applications for potential adjunct instructors who qualify to teach computer science courses. The Mathematics and Computer Science Department is looking for a part-time faculty member available to teach a variety of courses in computer science. In the Spring 2027 term, an instructor who can teach Programming for the Internet (online course) and/or Programming and Problem Solving (in-person course) is the immediate need. Salary Range: Salary is dependent on education and experience, in accordance with the Minnesota State College Faculty [MSCF] bargaining agreement (available on the Minnesota State website or by clicking here ). The range for this position is $43,067 - $98,660. Official transcripts and job verification required upon hire. The position also includes excellent fringe benefits. Per MSCF Contract, Adjuncts are assigned a per credit rate that is determined by the school. Minimum Qualifications Master's degree with a major in Computer Science, or Master's degree in any discipline/field with a minimum of 18 graduate semester credits (27 graduate quarter credits) in computer science. Preferred Qualification Previous teaching experience in Computer Science is highly desired. Recent industry experience in Computer Science, Information Technology, and/or Cybersecurity highly desired. Industry recognized certifications Experience teaching at a two-year college level Application Procedures Applications will ONLY be accepted through the online application process. No paper applications will be considered. Attach a resume and a cover letter. Official Transcripts and Certifications will be required if hired. Interviews The college will schedule interviews after initial screening of applications. Initial screening will begin on 11/16/2026. Work Shift (Hours / Days of work) Exempt - typical work week Monday-Friday, 8am-4:30pm Telework (Yes/No) At RCTC, occasional and situational telework is welcomed for some roles. Our aim is to ensure that the needs of our students, employees, and the College are consistently met. This position is based at RCTC in Rochester, Minnesota, where relationships and the needs of our employees matter. About Established in 1915, RCTC is the largest higher education provider in the fastest-growing city in Minnesota, serving more than 7,500 students a year in credit courses and nearly 4,000 in non-credit continuing and workforce education programs. RCTC combines the best in liberal arts, technical, and life- long learning with more than 70 credit-based programs and over 100 credential options. RCTC’s expansive 518-acre campus includes university partnerships, a diverse student body, and a vibrant student life program. RCTC provides a unique learning environment that offers the feel of a four-year university campus with the commitment to access and opportunity of a two-year college. RCTC is a member of Minnesota State—a higher education system that includes 24 two-year community and technical colleges and seven state universities serving more than 430,000 students. It is the fifth- largest higher education system of its kind in the United States. jobs.title: Contracted Faculty of Practice (Adjunct): Biology Labs
jobs.description: Home Position: Contracted Faculty of Practice (Adjunct): Biology Labs Location: St. Paul, MN Job Id: BIO # of Openings: 6 Position Overview: Faculty at Concordia University, St. Paul work as members of an academic team of full- and part-time colleagues to consistently deliver high-quality instruction to students. Faculty are expected to demonstrate innovation and excellence in course instruction, foster an atmosphere of active intellectual and creative engagement with students in and out of the classroom, and support the Christian mission of the university. With students at the center of the university’s mission, delivering a high-quality student experience is a top priority of the Concordia learning community. Course Description: BIO 120 General Biology I - This course emphasizes inquiry and investigation while introducing students to the unifying theories of modern biological science. Topics considered include foundational mechanisms of matter, energy, cells, genetics, and reproduction. BIO 315 Human Anatomy and Physiology I- This course is part one of a study of the structure and function of the human body. Major topics include the introduction to the human body, cells, tissues and skeletal, muscle, and nervous systems. BIO 316 Human Anatomy and Physiology II- This course is part two of a study of the structure and function of the human body. Major topics include the endocrine, cardiovascular, respiratory, digestive, reproductive and urinary systems. Class Dates/Times: 1/11/2027-5/5/2027 BIO 120 General Biology I ​Thursdays from 9:00 AM to 10:50 AM Thursdays from 12:00 PM to 1:50 PM BIO 315 Human Anatomy and Physiology I ​Tuesdays from 9:00 AM to 10:50 AM Tuesdays from 12:00 PM to 1:50 PM Tuesdays from 2:00 PM to 3:50 PM BIO 316 Human Anatomy and Physiology II ​Thursdays from 12:00 PM to 1:50 PM Pre-Written Course: Yes Modality: In-person # of Credits: 1-2 credits per section Total Compensation: $1,250 per credit Program/College: Biology; College of Business, Science, and Technology Course Instruction Responsibilities: Facilitate quality student learning through teaching assigned courses. Course topics include, but are not limited to, College Algebra, Precalculus, Calculus I/II, Statistics, and Discrete Math. The candidate is expected to contribute to further develop current and future programs; advise students; engage in department and campus service activities; participate in recruitment and retention efforts; and help expand our network with the industry to benefit our programs, student experience, and student employment opportunities. Additional teaching responsibilities could include courses within the Software Engineering program, with appropriate candidate expertise. The candidate will be expected to teach both on-campus and online courses. Qualifications MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS:Master’s degree in Mathematics or closely related field (or a master’s degree, plus a minimum of 18 graduate credits in Mathematics); passion for teaching and student-centered service; ability to relate complex concepts to diverse audiences; demonstrated cultural competency; effective communication skills; and commitment to an experiential educational philosophy within the scope of the land-grant mission. The final job offer is contingent upon receipt of official transcripts, a complete background check, and authorization to work in the United States. PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:Doctorate in Mathematics or closely related field, full-time teaching experience in an academic institution, and experience with online education. Candidates possessing current mathematics teaching licensure are especially encouraged to apply. About the Department The University of Minnesota Crookston (UMC) is one of five campuses comprising the University of Minnesota system. UMC is a four-year public university with an enrollment of 1,900 students, approximately half on campus and half in online degrees. The student body is diverse and comes from over 40 states and over 30 countries. Thirty-four baccalaureate degrees are offered, 15 of which are also offered online. UMC proudly carries on a tradition of over a century of educational service to northwestern Minnesota, beginning in 1906 as a regional residential high school, changing to a two-year college in 1966 and to a four-year college in 1993. Since 1993, UMC has equipped all on-campus students and faculty with laptop computers in a technology-rich environment. UMC is a small student-centered community of learning and scholars known for providing personal attention to every student. UMC makes a commitment to each individual student’s achievements and offers a hands-on approach and experiential learning that put students ahead of the competition. Integral to the university's statewide land-grant mission, UMC provides applied, career-oriented learning programs including internships and connects its teaching, research, and outreach to local, county, and regional economic development agencies in support of the global economy. UMC delivers world‐class University of Minnesota degrees in an affordable, close‐knit campus setting where faculty and staff personally invest in the success of each student. jobs.title: Physician – Interventional Psychiatrist (Assistant Professor)
jobs.description: Previous JobJob TitlePhysician – Interventional Psychiatrist (Assistant Professor) Next JobApply for JobJob ID376794 LocationTwin Cities Job FamilyAcademic Full/Part TimeFull-Time Regular/TemporaryRegular Job Code9403 Employee ClassInstr Fac/TC and Coord Cmp Add to My Favorite JobsEmail this Job About the Job The University of Minnesota’s Department of Psychiatry & Behavioral Sciences is seeking an Outpatient Psychiatry Physician for a clinical track faculty position at the Assistant, Associate or Full Professor level. The 0.9 clinical FTE will provide care within the Interventional Psychiatry services. The psychiatrist will perform evaluations and treatment of patients with Treatment Resistant Depression (TRD) including Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation (TMS), Electroconvulsive Therapy (ECT), Vagus Nerve Stimulation (VNS), ketamine and psychedelics at MHealth Fairview. The ideal candidate has experience in interventional psychiatry and an academic health center supporting residency education in a clinical setting. This is a unique opportunity to combine delivery of care with education on effective outcomes and development of care delivery systems in a nationally recognized premiere interventional psychiatry clinical and research service. The faculty member in this role will exercise creativity in clinical care and clinical programming, will teach and supervise outstanding trainees including Neuromodulation Medicine fellows, and will have the opportunity for involvement in research. Position Highlights: ●0.10 FTE (equivalent to 4 hours per week) of Academic activities, including publishing, research, mentoring, quality improvement projects, and other scholarly duties (meetings, grand rounds, committees, etc.). ●0.9 (equivalent to 36 hours per week) clinical FTE will provide care within the MHealth Saint Louis Park clinic and provide ECT services at UMMC Riverside. This work will be a combination of supervising residents and medical students, with individual care delivery and program building. The ideal candidate has previous experience and expertise in working with treatment resistant depression, anxiety disorders, and management in the delivery of care. Job Responsibilities: Provide professional psychiatric adult outpatient services for the University of Minnesota St. Louis Park clinic and at the UMMC West Bank Hospital. Work with the outpatient team and clinical leadership to provide evidence-based outpatient services. Work collaboratively with leadership to achieve the missions of clinical, education, and research. Partner with administrative leadership to maintain and constantly improve high-quality, patient-centered care and expand interventional psychiatry services at the University of Minnesota. Lead by example and engage learners and staff in creating a positive work environment that values excellence and teamwork and continually strives to exceed patient and family expectations. Reporting Relationships: 1. Primary reporting relationship to the Adult Mental Health Division Director. 2. Clinical care reports to the Medical and or Mental Health Directors of the UMN St. Louis Park Clinic. Qualifications Required Qualifications: ●Graduate of an accredited ACGME Psychiatry training program. ●Board eligible/certified with the ABMS. ●Licensed or ability to obtain a medical license and DEA in the State of Minnesota and meet threshold criteria/qualifications for credentialing and privileges. ●Demonstrated knowledge and training in clinical interventional psychiatry. ●Ability to receive work authorization in the United States from the U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services and maintain legal status according to the requirements of the visa category while in the United States. jobs.description: SUMMARY Own the process of recruiting and preparing TELL Network instructors to teach confidently and consistently while assisting with student and class administration as needed. This position takes prospective instructors from initial interest through screening, approval handoff, onboarding, training, technical readiness, and ongoing support. The position also supports communication and administrative workflow between students and instructors to help classes operate efficiently. This role maintains instructor-facing content and digital resources by updating training presentations, instructional materials, and selected website content as program needs evolve while supporting student operations. The result is a dependable pool of trained instructors and well-supported students progressing through the TELL program toward church planting. ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES Instructor Recruitment and Onboarding Recruit prospective TELL Network English instructors through approved campaigns, ministry networks, referrals, and follow-up activities. Serve as the primary contact for prospective and newly approved instructors throughout recruitment and onboarding. Conduct initial screening and route candidates through the established approval process; clearly document who has been approved to proceed. Guide approved instructors through a consistent onboarding process covering the TELL Network program, student path, LIVE Class expectations, instructor responsibilities, and communication standards. Maintain an onboarding checklist and track each instructor from initial interest through ready-to-teach status. Confirm when an instructor has completed readiness requirements and communicate that status promptly to the Student Operations & Scheduling Coordinator. Training and Teaching Readiness Train instructors in Zoom, class-flow expectations, WhatsApp communication, attendance procedures, student follow-up, safeguarding of student information, and other tools or processes used in LIVE Classes. Maintain and improve instructor training materials, quick-reference guides, checklists, FAQs, and other support resources. Update instructor-facing PowerPoint presentations and other digital teaching resources to reflect approved curriculum, process, and program changes. Make routine content updates to TELL Network website pages related to instructor resources, training, events, and other assigned program information; coordinate platform, design, integration, or significant website changes with the Digital Marketing & Technology Manager; and monitor and respond to instructor-related TELL Network email inquiries. Help instructors understand how each class fits into the larger TELL Network student path and how their teaching and communication support student momentum. Communicate approved process changes and updated expectations to active instructors. Maintain clear readiness standards and identify additional preparation required before an instructor is listed as ready for assignment. Ongoing Instructor/Student Support Provide ongoing support to active instructors regarding class expectations, student communication, attendance, follow-up, and common teaching or administrative questions. Assist instructors with routine technical difficulties before or during class and escalate unresolved system, integration, or platform issues to the Digital Marketing & Technology Manager through the established support process. Maintain substitute and emergency-readiness options when feasible and communicate urgent staffing risks to the Student Operations & Scheduling Coordinator. Encourage instructor engagement and re-engage trained instructors who have become inactive when additional teachers are needed. jobs.description: Previous JobJob TitleVisiting Assistant Professor Next JobApply for JobJob ID376426 LocationTwin Cities Job FamilyAcademic Full/Part TimeFull-Time Regular/TemporaryRegular Job Code9403V Employee ClassInstr Fac/TC and Coord Cmp Add to My Favorite JobsEmail this Job About the Job University of Minnesota Law SchoolVisiting Assistant Professorship ProgramVisiting Assistant Professor, 9403V Visiting Assistant Professor (VAP) Program In 2025, the University of Minnesota Law School launched a new program for law school graduates and practicing lawyers aspiring to become legal academics. The Visiting Assistant Professor (VAP) program is designed to give participants the resources, mentorship, teaching experience, and intellectual community they need to develop an ambitious scholarly agenda and prepare for the law school teaching market. Minnesota VAPs presumptively spend three years in the program. They are expected to teach one or two law school classes per year and develop a body of scholarship in anticipation of entering the law school teaching market in their second or third year.VAPs participate fully in the intellectual life of Minnesota Law. Each VAP is paired with a faculty mentor who provides sustained guidance on scholarship, teaching, professional development, and the academic job market. VAPs participate in the weekly faculty colloquium and are invited to attend the Law School’s workshops in legal history, public law, and law and technology, which bring scholars from around the country to present their research. VAPs join a large community of scholars at different stages of their careers, including other VAPs and junior scholars who regularly present their research to one another at junior faculty workshops. As part of a major research university, VAPs are also encouraged to build relationships with scholars beyond the Law School, including in the Medical School, School of Public Health, Humphrey School of Public Affairs, Carlson School of Management, College of Liberal Arts, and departments and programs in fields such as economics, history, philosophy, political science, psychology, sociology, and the sciences. Duties / ResponsibilitiesVAPs are expected to teach a two-credit seminar of their own design in the spring semester of their first academic year in the VAP program. In their second year, VAPs are expected to teach five credits, likely the same seminar taught in Year One plus a three-credit doctrinal class. In their third year, VAPs will teach three credits, ordinarily in the spring semester to facilitate the academic job market.VAPs are expected to make substantial progress on an independent research agenda and to complete at least one full-length scholarly article suitable for publication and capable of serving as a job-talk paper. AppointmentThis is a 100% time, renewable, 12-month academic professional appointment which will begin in summer 2027. The initial appointment will be for a period of one year. The appointment may be renewed for up to an additional two years following the successful completion of the first year. The position is onsite at the University of Minnesota School of Law in Minneapolis, MN.CompensationVAPs will be paid an annual salary of $75,000. The Law School will also provide professional and scholarly development support, including resources for research assistants, membership in professional associations, and participation in scholarly conferences. Qualifications Required QualificationsJ.D. degree from an A.B.A. accredited law school. Applicants must have a demonstrated interest in pursuing legal academia.
